$comment: Negative fixture for RFC-AITP-0005 §5.3 (proposal #72 Item 5). The token is a standard mint (`__JWS_TCT__`) signed by kat-keypair-001, which is also `sub` and `aud`, so `aud` equals `expected_audience` and the signature verifies. The claims are schema-valid (the schema cannot express `iss != sub`), so the map entry is `expect: valid`.
description: A self-issued TCT (`iss == sub`) presented in a grant context MUST be rejected with TCT_SIGNATURE_INVALID (RFC-AITP-0005 §5.3, §7.2 step 5). agentA signs a TCT naming itself as issuer, subject and audience, carrying an ordinary capability grant. Its signature verifies and every other claim is well formed. `verify_tct` evaluates the token as a capability grant, and no agent can grant capabilities to itself. A verifier that checks only the signature and `aud` accepts it.

expected.rationale: RFC-AITP-0005 §5.3: in a grant context, a TCT with `iss` equal to `sub` MUST be rejected with TCT_SIGNATURE_INVALID, the structural-rejection code (registries/error-codes.md). It is not AUDIENCE_MISMATCH: `aud` matches `expected_audience`. RFC-AITP-0006 §4 step 8 and RFC-AITP-0011 §3 give the same rule for delegation, so the signature-family code is consistent across both grant paths.
